scenes.tts: Marine threespine sticklebacks have a pelvis with two spines. In Paxton Lake, the bottom-feeding fish have a greatly reduced pelvis, and most have no pelvic bones at all. The gene most strongly tied to the difference is Pit X one. Yet its protein is unchanged in the fish examined. How can a body part shrink while its gene still makes a normal protein?

scenes.tts: Pit X one makes a protein that binds DNA, and mice without it have malformed hind limbs. But a gene can have several switches, called enhancers. An enhancer is a short stretch of noncoding DNA that raises a gene's use in particular tissues. One switch can serve the jaw, another the pelvis. Break the pelvic switch, and the jaw light stays on.

scenes.tts: Mapping found a region near the gene, but a region can hold many genes. The change might sit beside the gene, in cis, or in another gene that supplies its regulators, in trans. A hybrid can tell them apart. Each hybrid cell holds a marine allele and a Paxton allele, two versions of the gene, in one nucleus. Both meet the same transcription factors.
scenes.visual: Chromosome with a mapped region and the Pitx1 gene; cis and trans questions; then one nucleus holding a marine and a Paxton allele with shared factors.

scenes.tts: In an invented example, ninety percent of pelvic transcripts come from the marine allele. Ten percent come from the Paxton allele, and in the jaw the split is fifty fifty. The factors are shared, so the Paxton allele itself is less active: a change in cis, only in the pelvis. In 2010, Chan and colleagues ran the real version in hybrids. The Paxton allele was lower in pelvic tissue, but not in head tissue.
scenes.visual: Invented split bars for pelvis (90:10) and jaw (50:50), the cis verdict; then the real 2010 result as two tiles.

scenes.tts: That study also found Pel, an enhancer upstream of the gene. In a reporter assay, a sequence is joined to a visible marker and placed in embryos. Marine Pel drove pelvic expression, but the Paxton version, which carried a deletion, gave none in eight transgenic fish tested. A reporter shows only what a sequence can drive, not that form depends on it. Rescue comes closer: a marine Pel Pit X one minigene variably enhanced pelvic spines in Bear Paw Lake fry.

scenes.tts: Deleting the enhancer Pel B in mice left about eighty-five percent of hind-limb Pit X one RNA. Several bones were shorter, and this enhancer tunes how much Pit X one the limb makes. Mapping localises, in situ hybridization shows where the transcript is, and the hybrid test separates cis from trans. A reporter shows what a sequence can drive, and a native deletion tests whether form depends on it. Each method answers its own question.
